description: Pinned tool artifacts for the personal-dotfiles bootstrap on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 x amd64/arm64. Every download is checked against the recorded sha256 (or sha512 for npm) before anything is extracted, and a mismatch fails the install. Versions change only by editing this file.

keys.placeholders: {home}, {data_home}, {codex_home} come from installer/platform.Target and $CODEX_HOME (default {home}/.codex). {prefix_root} and {bin_dir} are the top-level values below. {version} is the entry's version, {target} the selected artifact's target, {prefix} the entry's resolved prefix, {download} the verified local download, {keyring} a private keyring built from the pinned signer key. Nothing here is a host path.
keys.prefix_root: Installer-owned root. Each tool lives in its own versioned directory beneath it, so an upgrade is a new directory plus a link switch.
keys.bin_dir: Installer-owned directory of symlinks into the tool prefixes. The shell configuration adds it to PATH explicitly.
keys.tools.<id>.artifacts: Keyed by dpkg architecture (amd64, arm64). url is the exact download, sha256 the expected digest, archive the format, strip_components how many leading directories to drop on extraction.
keys.tools.<id>.integrity: Where the recorded digests came from and what, if anything, authenticates that source. checksum_source.type is one of: signed-checksum-file, signed-manifest, checksum-file, github-release-asset-digest, npm-registry-integrity.
keys.tools.<id>.install: method is one of: extract (unpack into prefix), vendor-self-install (run the verified binary's own install subcommand), npm-global-prefix (npm install --global --prefix).
keys.tools.<id>.links: Link name in bin_dir -> path relative to the prefix.
keys.tools.<id>.verify: argv to run after installation, and a regular expression its stdout must match. Runs with a clean HOME in tests; must not need authentication or network.
keys.tools.<id>.verification: What was actually checked on 2026-09-28 and where. arm64 artifacts were never executed on this amd64 host.
keys.home_links: bin_dir link names that must also resolve outside zsh (systemd, GUI launchers, non-login shells). The packages phase returns them as symlink requests for {home}/.local/bin -> {bin_dir}/<name>; the dotfiles transaction owns those links.
keys.python_venvs: Installer-owned virtual environments. pip runs only inside them (PIP_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null, PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV=1); never --user, never --break-system-packages. only_binary refuses source builds, since no compiler is installed.
keys.tools.<id>.group: packages.json group the tool belongs to; default shell-core.

nvim.note: pynvim is not version-pinned; the installed version is recorded in the phase details and state.

node.channel: Active LTS 'Krypton' (maintenance from 2026-10-20, end of life 2028-04-30)
node.selection: Newest LTS line satisfying oh-my-codex engines.node '>=20'. Node 26 is not LTS until 2026-10-28; Node 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30.

integrity.note: The signer is the Node.js releaser who built v24.21.0 and is listed in the nodejs/node README release keys. gpgv (always present with apt) is enough; gnupg is not required.

verification.amd64: PASS: downloaded, sha256 matched SHASUMS256.txt, SHASUMS256.txt.sig verified with gpgv against the pinned key, node --version = v24.21.0 and bundled npm 11.19.0 ran on an amd64 host.
verification.arm64: Checksum entry present in the signed SHASUMS256.txt; URL answered HTTP 200. Execution UNVERIFIED.

neovim.selection: nvim/init.lua disables plugins below 0.11 and warns below 0.12; etc/install-neovim.sh recommends 0.12.2. 0.12.5 is the current stable release.

integrity.note: Neovim 0.12.x releases publish no checksum file or signature; the recorded digests are GitHub's server-side sha256 for the uploaded assets. This authenticates the transfer against the pinned value, not the publisher.

caveats: nvim/lua/config/treesitter.lua uses nvim-treesitter main, which compiles extra parsers with the tree-sitter CLI and a C compiler. Neither is installed, so only the bundled parsers are available.
nvim/lua/config/pynvim.lua may try to install pynvim with pip; that conflicts with the venv-only Python policy and needs a decision in the editor lane.

verification.amd64: PASS: downloaded, sha256 matched the recorded asset digest, nvim --version = v0.12.5 and a headless run with a temporary HOME reported has('nvim-0.12') = 1.
verification.arm64: Asset digest recorded from the GitHub release API; URL answered HTTP 200. Execution UNVERIFIED.

fzf.selection: Needs >= 0.66 for fzf --raw (zsh/zsh.d/alias.zsh), --accept-nth (bin/tmux-attach) and --tmux popups (tmux/tmux.conf, bin/tmux-attach). Built-in `fzf --zsh` integration replaces the ~/.fzf clone that upstream install.py used.

fzf-preview.sh.reason: tmux/tmux.conf prefix-@ picker previews with fzf-preview.sh, which is not in the release tarball.

integrity.note: Unsigned checksum file published with the release; its entries equal GitHub's asset digests. fzf-preview.sh is pinned by tag and sha256 only.

verification.amd64: PASS: downloaded, sha256 matched the checksum file, fzf --version = 0.74.4, fzf --zsh produced integration code, --accept-nth and --raw were accepted. On a tmux 3.2a server fzf --tmux failed (display-popup usage error); on tmux 3.4 the options were accepted but no popup was rendered because no client was attached (UNVERIFIED rendering).
verification.arm64: Checksum entry present in the checksum file; URL answered HTTP 200. Execution UNVERIFIED.

integrity.sigstore_bundles: codex-package-<target>.tar.gz.sigstore is published next to each archive. Checking it needs cosign or sigstore tooling, which this profile does not install, so it is not part of the default verification.
integrity.note: This is the same archive and checksum file the official install.sh uses. The installer does not run install.sh, because install.sh edits shell profile files that this repository manages.

codex.self_update: Codex's own updater manages {codex_home}/packages/standalone; it does not manage this prefix. Upgrades go through this manifest.

verification.amd64: PASS: downloaded, sha256 matched codex-package_SHA256SUMS, codex --version = codex-cli 0.157.1 with an empty temporary HOME and CODEX_HOME (it warned that CODEX_HOME did not exist, and wrote nothing else).
verification.arm64: Checksum entry present in codex-package_SHA256SUMS; URL answered HTTP 200. Execution UNVERIFIED.

claude-code.selection: Current 'stable' channel build (downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/stable). The 'latest' channel was 2.1.283 on 2026-09-28.
claude-code.license: Proprietary (Anthropic). Not redistributed; downloaded from Anthropic on the target.

steps: download manifest.json and manifest.json.sig; gpgv against the pinned key
read platforms.<platform>.checksum and size from the verified manifest and compare with this entry
download the binary to a private temporary directory; check size and sha256
run '<binary> install 2.1.274'; delete the temporary binary
install.no_pipe_to_shell: claude.ai/install.sh is not executed. It always resolves 'latest' for its own download and then runs the same install subcommand.

claude-code.auto_update: The native build updates itself in the background. The recorded stable channel keeps it on the delayed track; DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 or DISABLE_UPDATES stop it, which is a user setting decision, not set here.

verification.amd64: PASS: manifest.json.sig verified with gpgv against key 31DDDE24DDFAB679F42D7BD2BAA929FF1A7ECACE (fingerprint matches the setup documentation), binary sha256 matched the manifest, claude --version = 2.1.274, and 'claude install 2.1.274' in a temporary HOME created only the vendor_layout paths and left sentinel .zshrc, .bashrc and .profile byte-identical.
verification.arm64: Checksum present in the signed manifest; URL answered HTTP 200 with the manifest's size. Execution UNVERIFIED.

oh-my-codex.selection: npm dist-tag latest (published 2026-09-21). The source machine ran 0.20.5; both declare the same engines.

integrity.provenance: The registry lists npm publish and SLSA v1 provenance attestations for this version; 'npm audit signatures' can check them.
integrity.note: Install from the verified local tarball so the top-level package cannot differ from the pinned integrity. npm checks every dependency tarball against registry integrity, but a global install has no lockfile, so transitive versions resolve within their semver ranges at install time.

native.note: Prebuilt N-API binaries selected by npm through optionalDependencies (os/cpu/libc). No node-gyp and no compiler.

dependencies.install_scripts: Only oh-my-codex itself has one (postinstall). No dependency declares install scripts.

postinstall.runs_when: npm_config_global is true (a --global install); otherwise it is a no-op.
postinstall.effect: Downloads the omx-runtime native helper for the platform from the matching GitHub release, checking sha256 from native-release-manifest.json. Failures are non-fatal (native runtime features stay off).

install.path: {bin_dir}:/usr/bin:/bin for npm and omx, so the pinned node is used rather than any system or nvm node.

verification.amd64: PASS: tarball sha512 matched dist.integrity; an isolated --ignore-scripts install into a temporary prefix (temporary npm cache, no user config) resolved 112 packages; omx --version printed 'oh-my-codex v0.21.6' with an empty temporary HOME; the amd64 omx-runtime archive matched its manifest sha256. The postinstall hydration itself was not run.
verification.arm64: Package is architecture independent. arm64 native lzma integrity and omx-runtime sha256 recorded; both URLs answered HTTP 200. Execution UNVERIFIED.

nerd-font.selection: zsh/p10k.zsh sets POWERLEVEL9K_MODE=nerdfont-complete and tmux/statusbar.tmux uses private-use glyphs; the README recommends JetBrainsMono Nerd Font. Only needed where a GUI terminal renders text.

verification.any: Archive downloaded and sha256 matched SHA-256.txt; it contains 96 TTF files plus OFL.txt and README.md. Font installation and rendering in GNOME Terminal UNVERIFIED.
